title: SC Amplifiers and Integrators
intro: Capacitor ratios on a chip are accurate to 0.1 percent, much better than absolute values, so SC circuits give precise gain.

blocks.text: A capacitor C switched between two nodes at frequency fclk transfers a charge C*(V1 - V2) per cycle, an average current C*fclk*(V1 - V2). It behaves like a resistor Req = 1/(fclk * C). A 1 pF capacitor at 1 MHz emulates 1 Mohm in a tiny area.
In the sampling phase the input capacitor C1 samples Vin; in the amplify phase its charge is moved onto the feedback capacitor C2 around an op amp. The gain is C1/C2 and depends only on a ratio.

The same circuit, with C2 not discharged between clocks, accumulates the charge: each cycle adds ΔVout = -(Cs/CF) * Vin. The ideal transfer function is H(z) = -(Cs/CF) * z^-1 / (1 - z^-1), an accumulator. It is the building block of switched-capacitor filters and delta-sigma modulators.
Each clock adds a fixed step; the slope of the staircase is Cs/CF times Vin. Reverse the sign of Vin to run the staircase upward.
Capacitors that sample the output common-mode level and compare it with a reference, switched in the same two-phase manner, give a CMFB circuit without resistor loading on the output.
